2. The prosecution case arises out of a FIR lodged on 30-6-89 by Md. Belayet Hossain, Inspector of District Anti-Corruption Bureau, with police Station Nesarabad alleging, inter alia, that accused petitioner Amalendu Majumder was the Chairman of Gamudoy Khati Union Parishad and was also Chairman of a project Committee under the village works programme 1984-1985. Under the said programme Taka 63,595.00 was alloted to the petitioner for reconstruction of an iron bridge adjacent to Kundudaskati Government Primary School. It is alleged that the petitioner completed work upto Taka 34,491.00 and misappropriated the remaining amount of Taka 25,503.00 in his capacity as the Chairman of the Project Committee. On this allegation the aforesaid Nesarabad PS Case No. 2 dated 30-6-89 under section 409 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 was registered. The police took up investigation of the case on 30-6-89 and the learned Magistrate by his order dated 27-12-89 extended a period of 30 days for investigation which, according to the accused- petitioner, expired on 26-1-90. It is alleged that the Investigating officer without obtaining any permission either from the learned Magistrate or learned Sessions Judge continued the investigation for a period of two years and this was illegally allowed by the learned Magistrate. It is further alleged that the case was pending for obtaining santion from the appropriate authority/and on 27-6-91 the investigating officer violating the provisions of section 167 of the CrPC and without obtaining any sancction from the appropriate authority submitted charge sheet under section 409 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. The grievance of the petitioner is that the learned Magistrate most illegally accepted the charge sheet on 4-7-91 beyond the time limit of 180 days as provided under section 5A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. It is on this allegation that the accused-petitioner filed this revisional application under section 561A of CrPC and obtained the present Rule. 

 3. Mr. Syed Ziaul Karim, learned Advocate appearing for the accused-petitioner, submits that the acceptance of the charge sheet by the learned Magistrate under his order dated 4-7-91 is bad in law inasmuch as the charge-sheet was submitted beyond the time limit of 180 days as provided in section 5A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958. He submits that the order of the learned Magistrate accepting the charge sheet suffers from infirmity, because the charge sheet was submitted by the investigating officer after 180 days without obtaining any permission from the learned Sessions Judge and, as such, the proceedings of the said case pending before the learned Magistrate are illegal and without jurisdiction and liable to be quashed as such. 

 4. We may quote section 5A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 (XL of 1958) as amended by the Criminal Law Amendment (Amendment) Act, 1987, which came into force with effect from 20-1-87. Section 5A of the Act reads as follows: 

 5. This means that the period of investigation for an offence under the Criminal Law Amendment, Act, 1958 is one hundred and eighty days. 

 6. We may quote section 6(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, which reads as follows: 

 7. It is clear from this that the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Code have been made applicable to the proceedings of the court of a Special Judge in so far as the provisions of the Code are not inconsistent with the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. This means that for the purpose of investigation, the provisions of section 167 of the CrPC are applicable prescribing a time limit of 180 days for completing the investigation. Now the question is: What will be the consequence if the charge sheet could not be submitted by the investigating officer within a period of 180 days? We do not find in the record any information if the investigation officers obtained permission from the learned Session Judge for completing the investigation beyond 180 days. We, however, find from their order sheet submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the charge sheet was accepted by the learned Magistrate under his order dated 4-7-91 and the FIR was lodged on 30-6-89.
